schema.description: One gym visit, from a records file: the statement that a visit happened, with as much detail as the source has. The Strong extract (scripts/extract-strong-csv.py) wrote one per workout until Strong moved to activity.exercise-session; a hand-kept row may say no more than the day. Values are the source's own. Version 2 requires source_time, every other rule unchanged. No writer sends this type any more: Strong moved to activity.exercise-session.strong, and no records file holds a gym visit.

activity.description: What was done, in words. The Strong extract wrote "strength training"; a hand-kept row says it its own way.

app.description: The app that logged the workout, "Strong" for rows from the Strong extract.

avg_watts.description: Average power in watts, as written in the hand-kept note.

date.description: When the visit started, local Sydney time to the minute. This is the fact time. With time_unknown, the time is a placeholder.

distance_m.description: Distance covered in metres, as written in the hand-kept note.

duration.description: How long the whole session took, warm-up and cool-down included, as the hand-kept note wrote it: minutes, seconds and tenths (m:ss.t). Kept as text, not converted.

duration_sec.description: Strong's "Duration (sec)" for the workout, as reported. Strong leaves a workout open until the next starts, so it can be far too long.

exercises.description: The workout's exercise names in the order Strong first lists them, from the "Exercise Name" column.

id.description: The records row's id. The Strong extract wrote strong: and the workout's start; a hand-kept row has its own.

max_watts.description: Peak power in watts, as written in the hand-kept note.

sets.description: Every row of the Strong workout in file order, set by set, rest timers and notes included.

items.description: One Strong CSV row, minus the workout-level columns.

rpe.description: The "RPE" column, the rating of perceived exertion as logged.

seconds.description: The "Seconds" column, a timed set's length in seconds.

set.description: The "Set Order" column as text: a set number, or a marker such as "Rest Timer" or "Note" for rows that are not sets.

split_500m.description: Pace per 500 m as the hand-kept note wrote it, in minutes, seconds and tenths followed by words naming the stretch it covers, which can be the work interval rather than the whole session. Kept as text.

started.description: Strong's "Date" column, the workout's start to the second, local time. Strong rows only.

time_unknown.description: True when the source gave the day but no time, so date carries midnight as a placeholder.

workout_notes.description: The workout's distinct "Workout Notes" values, sorted.

source_time.description: How the visit's clock was read: value is date, the visit's start as a wall clock with no zone, read in Australia/Sydney, the Definition's zone. The Strong extract (version 1) wrote local time without a zone, so a facet says basis assumption, or configuration where a person's setting names the zone. No writer sends this type any more; a facet written again must say how its clock was read.

value.description: The fact time as the source supplied it, as text and never rewritten: a date, a wall clock, an RFC 3339 string, or an epoch as its digits.

zone.description: The zone value is read in, and nothing else: an IANA name when one is known, UTC for a value that is UTC, else a fixed offset +HH:MM or -HH:MM. The gate refuses a name that is no zone.

basis.description: Who decided the zone. source: the source supplied it with the value, or the value is UTC by the source's own definition. configuration: a setting a person made for this source names it. assumption: the importer or writer chose it, with nothing behind it but its own default or the Definition's zone, and logged that it did.
